text:
linh: heads-up — trying a 'liquidation smoothing' pattern for preemptible GPUs. goal is to avoid hard-cut stream failures by bridging tokens + tiny warm standby pool. sketch below and tradeoffs.

ops-bot: AWS spot-interruption notice for instance i-0f12abcd (eu-west-1) — 2m remaining :warning:

mike: curious — what's different from our existing drain+requeue? sounds similar to previous proposals but with a standby pool.

linh: right — difference is two-fold: 1) token shadowing: mirror the streaming token state to a lightweight shadow stream that standby workers can pick up w/o full KV restore, 2) fractional warm standbys (small % of capacity) that accept resumed sessions for short time window to avoid client-visible failures.

raj: how do we keep KV/cache consistent? if standby picks up a stream and model needs KV, that would be expensive to rehydrate.

linh: idea is incremental prefix sync + small per-session delta logs. we only stream last N tokens + KV diffs. standby applies diffs and continues. fallback still requeues to primary if sync fails.

sara: do we have perf numbers on how long prefix sync takes for 1k token sessions? rough order-of-magnitude matters.

linh: quick bench on a V100-ish: streaming 1k tokens delta (only recent 256 tokens compressed) ~ 120–180ms in optimistic path. larger sessions add linearly but we only shadow recent working set.

mike: cost wise? warm standbys = idle GPUs. what's the incremental monthly cost if we keep 3% pool in us-west2?

linh: back-of-envelope: 3% of fleet translates to ~+2.8% infra spend (depends on instance types). but reduces tail-error risk and retries -> estimated net cost neutral for high-value customers. I can run a finer calc if we want.

devops: rollout question — can this be per-pool flag? we shouldn't force on all customers.

linh: yes, plan is opt-in per pool. config sample:

```json
{
  "standby_pool_fraction": 0.03,
  "preempt_grace_seconds": 45,
  "token_shadow_ttl_seconds": 90,
  "prefix_sync_window": 256
}
```

raj: edge-case: network partition during handoff — could cause duplicate token issuance or split-brain for stream ownership.

linh: agreed. mitigation: ephemeral lease with quick heartbeat; on ambiguous state we prefer safety -> reject takeover and requeue. also add idempotent token stamps so duplicate resumes are detected.

sara: can we simulate this in chaos test? kill nodes with 30s notice and measure client-visible errors + retries.

mike: also test with mixed-capacity pools (spot + on-demand) — ensure routing policy prefers on-demand for long-lived streams.

linh: rollout plan: PoC branch -> canary on non-prod -> perf/chaos -> opt-in beta customers -> GA. I'll open RFC and perf task this afternoon.

devops: please add a metric for 'handoff_success_rate' and 'shadow_sync_latency' so we can track regressions.

linh: noted. action items: lin h to open RFC (#rfc/infra) + perf task, devops to add metrics skeleton, sara to run chaos harness once PoC is up. thanks :thumbsup:
